title: ganja configuration
description: A ganja.toml file, read in three tiers — the global config home, the one file GANJA_CONFIG or --config names, then every directory from the working directory up to the project root — where later beats earlier. TOML is the only format: the retired ganja.jsonc / ganja.json names are refused at load, by extension rather than by whole file name, with a message naming the path and the `ganja config migrate` command that converts one. This schema is JSON because JSON Schema is, and it describes the value a config file decodes to rather than the syntax that spelled it — so an ordering or comment property of the TOML document is a property of the reader, not of the value. Taplo, the language server that completes a .toml file, reads this schema from a `#:schema <url>` directive on the document's first line. Every top-level key this build understands is listed here, and any other key is a hard load error naming it.
$comment: Derived from crates/ganja-core/src/config.rs:713-1045 (struct Config, #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]). Audited against config.rs and crates/ganja-core/tests/config_schema.rs, which catches drift in both directions.

$schema.description: Editor schema reference, curated so that writing one is not an error; nothing consults it. A quoted "$schema" key is legal TOML, so a file carrying one from before the format change still loads — but the way a TOML editor is pointed at this schema is taplo's `#:schema <url>` directive on the document's first line, not this key.

model.description: Default model, "provider/model", split on the first slash so openrouter/anthropic/claude-3 names the model anthropic/claude-3.

small_model.description: Cheaper model for the one request a session makes about itself: the title. Spelled `provider/model` like `model` and bound the same way — a spec naming another provider is left alone, and one the wire refuses falls back to the session's own model. Summaries are deliberately not included; they run on the turn's own model, as upstream's do.

default_provider.description: Provider a session runs as when no other tier names one: a builtin id or one declared in `provider`. It supplies only the provider; an id nothing ships or declares is refused at selection rather than at load.

effort.description: Catalog effort a fresh session starts under, as `/effort` and `run --effort` name them. A default and not an override: a resumed session runs under the effort its own row stored. A name the selected model's catalog row does not carry is cleared at adoption, never refused at load — which names exist depends on the model the other tiers settle on.

agent.description: Agent definitions, by name. A name nothing answers to becomes a new agent in mode "all"; a builtin's fields are replaced field by field.

agents.description: How this session runs the agents it has, as opposed to what they are (`agent`). Its own settings object beside the `agent` map rather than a key inside it, so a `concurrency` setting cannot collide with an agent actually named that.

teammates.description: How this session runs the teammates it spawns, as opposed to what they are. Plural for `agents`' reason: the singular is what a later per-name teammate map will want.

claude_code.description: How long the claude-code wire holds an idle claude process. Spelled with an underscore because this is a bare TOML key, where the wire's id (claude-code) is a value GANJA_PROVIDER and --model name.

cross_session_inbound.description: What this session, leading a team, does with a peer message arriving from outside that team: accept delivers it, hold parks it for a person's review, refuse drops it. Absent is unset — the engine then decides per receiver class, and an explicit value always wins over that default. The one key whose project tier diverges from later-beats-earlier: a project file replaces the standing value only when strictly more severe (accept < hold < refuse), so a checkout can tighten but never loosen, while the file GANJA_CONFIG names outranks the global config home ordinarily. Not a key a plugin can contribute.

dialog_expiry.description: How long a held peer message's review dialog waits for a person before it expires. Absent is "5m"; "never" is no deadline at all. Trusted tiers only — the global config home and the file GANJA_CONFIG names may set it, and a project file that sets it fails the load naming this key and that file: a checkout must not stretch or shrink the human review window. Not a key a plugin can contribute.

teamless_send.description: Whether a session that leads no team asks a person before its send_message leaves for another session: unasked sends as any tool call the rules allow, ask raises the ordinary permission dialog on each send. Absent is "unasked" — every cross-session delivery already terminates in the receiver's admission gate, cross_session_inbound's machinery, so the sender-side dialog is optional oversight rather than the boundary — and the key has no effect in a session that holds a team. Tighten-only in a project file (unasked < ask): a checkout can demand dialogs but never silence a person's ask, while the file GANJA_CONFIG names outranks the global config home ordinarily. Not a key a plugin can contribute. Live since D543: a session is teamless when its own registry holds no members, read at each call, so ask really does raise a dialog per send in a session that has spawned no teammate, and a teammate joining reverts it to the in-team ladder.

permission.description: Permission rules layered over the built-in ones.

instructions.description: Extra instruction files, as paths or globs. The one array that concatenates across tiers (order-preserving, deduplicated) rather than being replaced by the closest tier. An http(s) entry is skipped with a warning rather than fetched (D2).

theme.description: Theme by name: one of the ported builtins, or a theme file under <config home>/themes/.

theme_mode.description: Which variant of the selected theme to render.

keybinds.description: Key bindings, by action name. The value is one binding or several comma-separated alternatives ("ctrl+c,ctrl+q"); an empty value leaves the action reachable by no chord. Core keeps this map raw — the TUI resolves it and refuses an action name it does not have.
keybinds.$comment: Action names and their defaults: crates/ganja-tui/src/keybind.rs:48-86.

themes_open.description: Bound to nothing by default: ctrl+t went to the transcript overlay (D453). /themes and the palette still open it.

shell.description: Shell the `bash` tool runs commands in.

mcp.description: MCP servers this session may connect to, by name. The name is half of every tool those servers contribute (mcp__<server>__<tool>), so it is what a permission rule is written against.

tool_defer_threshold.description: Defer whole MCP servers' tool schemas (largest servers first) until the advertised mcp__* total is at or under this; a resident tool_search fetches a deferred schema on demand, and a direct call to a deferred tool still executes and activates it (D492). 0 defers every server; a huge value disables deferral. Absent = 32. Size is not coldness: the deferred giant may be the main server — its tools return to the roster the moment they are touched.

hooks.description: Commands this session runs at the nine moments the hook engine fires, keyed by the event's own spelling. An event name nothing answers to is refused by name at load. Hooks run with the user's own authority and pass no permission gate.

provider.description: Endpoints this build can talk to besides the ones it ships, by id, and — for the two ids that speak OpenAI's Responses API, chatgpt and openai — a curated `options` table for a builtin this build already ships (D563). The id is what GANJA_PROVIDER, --model <id>/…, `model` and a stored credential all name. Any other builtin id is refused at load, because such an entry would never be reached.

skills.description: Where this session looks for skills besides ganja's own two homes.

memory.description: Whether this session carries its project's own memory — a MEMORY.md index and the topic files beside it, kept under the project's data directory and maintained by the model through the ordinary file tools. tui.description: What the terminal frontend does beyond drawing frames. Parsed and refused-unknown in core like every other curated table, acted on only by the TUI.

openrouter.description: What the OpenRouter gateway is asked to run on its own side. Opt-in, because server tools bill per call (D489).

AgentConfig.title: Agent definition

prompt.description: System prompt, which replaces the base prompt rather than adding to it.

description.description: One line describing the agent, which the task tool shows the model.

hidden.description: A hidden agent exists but is not offered in a picker.

disable.description: A disabled agent is removed entirely.

permission.description: Rules layered over the built-in ones for calls this agent makes.

AgentsConfig.title: Agent execution settings
AgentsConfig.description: How this session runs the agents it has, rather than what they are. Not a key upstream has: upstream runs one subagent at a time, so it has nothing to size (D462).
AgentsConfig.$comment: crates/ganja-core/src/config.rs:739-751 (AgentsConfig, deny_unknown_fields); default of 4 at :764 (AgentsConfig::DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY); refusal of zero at :1728-1738 (check_agents).

concurrency.description: How many `task` calls from one assistant step may run at the same time. Absent is 4. Refused at load when it is zero — a cap of nothing is a session where every delegation hangs, which is not a thing anybody means to write.

TeammateConfig.title: Teammate execution settings
TeammateConfig.description: How this session runs the teammates it spawns, rather than what they are. Not a key upstream has, and not one Claude Code has either: only a headless foreign-CLI teammate had a turn ganja could not observe, so only that shape ever had anything to bound (D509). Since D512 every codex/agy/grok spawn opens the CLI's own native TUI in a tmux pane instead, and a pane is a thing a person can look at — so that key now governs the headless machinery alone, and is kept curated so a config file that already carries it still loads. The other keys: `shell` names the idle shell every pane teammate is spawned into (D520), and `pane_share` how wide the teammates' column opens (2026-08-25).
TeammateConfig.$comment: crates/ganja-core/src/config.rs (TeammateConfig, deny_unknown_fields); the per-CLI defaults live in crates/ganja-teammate-local/src/shim.rs; the pane-mode shape that reads none of this is crates/ganja-teammate-local/src/shim_tui.rs; refusal of zero in check_teammates.

shim_turn_timeout.description: How long one headless foreign-CLI teammate's turn may run, in seconds, before the shim ends its process group and mails the lead. Absent is the per-CLI default the shim derives; a value here overrides all three. Since D512 no spawn door in this build reaches that headless machinery — pane-mode shim teammates run no per-turn deadline and never read this key — so what a value here moves is the machinery the testkit still drives. Refused at load when it is zero — a deadline of nothing kills every headless turn before the child has written a byte.

shell.description: The shell a fresh teammate pane holds until its launch line is typed into it (D520), as a command line: "/bin/zsh -f", or just "/bin/bash". Absent is /bin/sh -s. Split into words as a shell would, and kept at two words or more by the pane door (-s is appended to a lone program), because tmux runs a one-word command through the login shell, whose startup files re-import what the enumerated environment withheld. A shell named here runs its own startup files too — the person's choice; -f (zsh) or --norc (bash) is how a shell is told not to. Must be a POSIX shell, since the launch line is typed as one reads it. Refused at load when empty or unsplittable.

pane_share.description: How much of the window's width the teammates' column takes when the first teammate opens it, in percent; the lead keeps the rest. Absent is 65 (lead 35 / teammates 65, 2026-08-25; 70 before that). Refused at load outside 1..=99, since a column of nothing or of everything leaves one side of the split with no screen.

ClaudeCodeConfig.title: claude-code wire settings
ClaudeCodeConfig.description: How long the claude-code wire keeps an idle claude process alive (D556). One key, and it is a trade rather than a tuning knob: the wire never passes --resume, so a held process is the conversation's memory of the assistant's own replies. Holding it costs the person's machine an authenticated node runtime; evicting it costs the model the words it said, because the fresh record that replaces it opens with an assistant-free preamble. No key upstream has: opencode ships no claude-code wire at all.
ClaudeCodeConfig.$comment: crates/ganja-core/src/config.rs (ClaudeCodeConfig, deny_unknown_fields); the default and the eviction it bounds live in crates/ganja-provider/src/provider/claude_code/held.rs (DEFAULT_IDLE_BOUND); refusal of zero in config::check_claude_code; the one reader is provider::select, which hands it to ClaudeCodeProvider::with_idle_bound.

idle_bound.description: How long a held claude process may sit idle before the wire closes it, in seconds. Absent is 600. Refused at load when it is zero, since a bound of nothing evicts every process before its first turn and no conversation would ever keep the assistant's words. A large value is not refused: spending the machine rather than the conversation is the trade this key exists to let a person make.

PermissionAction.title: Permission action
PermissionAction.description: What a rule does with the calls it covers: allow runs them unasked, ask puts them in front of the user, deny refuses them without a dialog. Any other string parses and is kept verbatim, and is treated as `ask` — a rule this build cannot carry out still says the call is not routine.
PermissionAction.$comment: crates/ganja-permission/src/permission.rs:416-432 (Action; Other(String) is #[serde(untagged)], so the vocabulary is open).

PermissionRuleSet.title: Permission rules for one tool
PermissionRuleSet.description: Either one action for every call to the tool ("bash": "ask"), or an action per call pattern in the order written ("bash": {"git *": "allow", "*": "ask"}). Order is semantic: the last matching rule wins.

PermissionConfig.title: Permission block
PermissionConfig.description: Either a bare action covering everything, or an object mapping tool names to rules. A bare action replaces everything below it instead of merging into it. Keys are tool ids — read, edit, write, glob, grep, bash, todowrite, webfetch, websearch, skill, question, task, plan_exit, bash_output, kill_shell, an mcp__<server>__<tool> name, or the pseudo-permission external_directory, which a call raises beside the tool's own when it would work outside the project.

CommandConfig.title: Custom command
CommandConfig.description: One custom slash command. Open to unknown keys.

template.description: The prompt the command sends, with $1..$N and $ARGUMENTS placeholders; a !`cmd` substitution runs at the project root and @file attaches like a composer mention.

description.description: One line describing it, shown in the palette.

agent.description: Agent the command runs as, when it should not run as the current one.

McpServer.description: One MCP server a session may connect to, tagged by `type`. An entry with no `type` is a parse error rather than a silently absent server.

McpRemote.description: An HTTP endpoint spoken to over streamable HTTP.

output_limit.description: Bytes one tool call to this server may return before the result is clamped. Absent gets the same budget every other tool in the registry answers to. Refused at load when it is zero — a byte budget of nothing refuses every result.

oauth.description: Discovers this server's own authorization server (RFC 8414) and logs in against it with dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) and PKCE, rather than a static `headers` entry carrying a fixed token. Absent means no login flow — `headers` is still the way to send a static credential.

McpOauth.title: MCP OAuth marker
McpOauth.description: Turns on OAuth discovery and dynamic registration for a remote MCP server. Carries nothing today — discovery finds the endpoints and dynamic registration finds the client — but is its own type rather than a bare boolean so a future field (a preregistered client_id, a scope) has somewhere to land without another migration of this shape. `oauth: {}` is the whole spelling; any key inside it is refused.

McpTimeout.title: MCP request budget
McpTimeout.description: Milliseconds one request to this server may take, governing requests only. Absent, a tool call gets 60000 and a tools/list gets 30000. The connect budget is a fixed 30000 and is never taken from here. Zero is not a value: the field is a non-zero integer.
McpTimeout.$comment: Defaults MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT / MCP_LIST_TIMEOUT / MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT at crates/ganja-core/src/config.rs:247, :250, :259.

ProviderConfig.title: Configured provider endpoint
ProviderConfig.description: One endpoint a config declares, and how to talk to it. There is deliberately no apiKey key: ganja's credentials travel the environment or auth.json, and `key_env` names the variable instead. Being selectable is not being cataloged — a configured provider has no sizing, pricing or auto-compaction, and must be told which model to ask for.

dialect.description: Which request/response mapping the endpoint speaks. Required: guessing it from a URL is how an Anthropic body reaches a chat-completions server.

base_url.description: Where it lives. Refused unless it is https, or http to loopback — the credential travels in a header on every request.

key_env.description: The environment variable holding the endpoint's key, consulted before the credential store. Absent means the store alone answers, under this entry's own id. A blank or whitespace-only value is refused, because it names no variable.

headers.description: Headers sent with every request, beside the credential.

Dialect.title: Wire dialect
Dialect.description: The wire a config-named endpoint speaks: POST {base}/chat/completions with a bearer token, POST {base}/responses with a bearer token (nothing sealed asked for, nothing replayed), or POST {base}/v1/messages with x-api-key and the pinned Anthropic version.

LspConfig.title: Language server configuration
LspConfig.description: true for the builtin servers, false for none, or a map of server names to entries merged over the builtins. Absent means the same as false. Across tiers two maps merge entry by entry and anything else replaces.

HookEventName.title: Hook event

NotificationEvent.description: One moment the TUI can announce: a turn finishing, or a permission or question dialog waiting for an answer.

NotificationMethod.title: Notification method
NotificationMethod.description: How an announcement reaches the terminal: OSC 9, which terminals that carry it surface as a desktop notification, or BEL, the terminal bell. The default is osc9 because of how it fails — a terminal that ignores it shows nothing, where an unwanted bell is a beep every turn.

BuiltinProviderEntry.title: Options for a builtin provider
BuiltinProviderEntry.description: A `provider` entry whose id names a wire this build already ships. It carries request options and nothing else — a builtin's endpoint, credential and headers all move with that builtin's own variables, so naming dialect, base_url, key_env or headers here is refused at load.

options.description: Curated Responses API request options for this id.

ResponsesOptions.title: Responses API request options
ResponsesOptions.description: What a request on the chatgpt or openai id carries beyond the conversation (D563). Every key is curated and refused by name at load, because the ChatGPT seat answers an unknown key with a 400 and the loader is the only place that can say so before a request is spent. Which of these keys each id accepts is narrower than this schema can express: the seat takes a measured subset and the loader refuses the rest naming the key, the id and the probe.
ResponsesOptions.$comment: crates/ganja-core/src/config.rs ResponsesOptions (deny_unknown_fields); per-id gate at check_responses_options against crates/ganja-provider/src/provider/responses/options.rs.

service_tier.description: How the turn is scheduled and billed. Measured as recognized rather than honored on the seat: every accepted value came back echoing default.

reasoning.description: How the model reasons, and how much of that reasoning comes back.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether the model may call several tools in one step.

tool_choice.description: What the model must call, if anything. The names inside an allowed_tools form are deliberately not checked at load: which tools a request offers is decided per turn.

custom_tools.description: Builtin tools to advertise as Responses custom tools beside their ordinary function entries, by registry name. Only a builtin with exactly one required string argument can be reached through a custom advertisement.

server_tools.description: Vendor-run tools, sent verbatim. Each one bills per call.

include.description: Extra response fields to ask for, unioned with the wire's own entries rather than replacing them.

context_management.description: Server-side transcript compaction, passed through. Independent of ganja's own compaction, which keeps running off the reported input tokens.

max_output_tokens.description: Ceiling on the tokens one response may generate. openai only — the seat rejects it.

max_tool_calls.description: Ceiling on the tool calls one response may make. openai only.

prompt_cache_key.description: Prompt-cache partition key. openai only: the seat replaces it with one of its own on every response.

prompt_cache_retention.description: How long the prompt cache keeps an entry. openai only.

top_logprobs.description: How many alternative tokens to report per position. openai only, and what message.output_text.logprobs comes back through.

truncation.description: What to do with a request that overflows the window. openai only.

safety_identifier.description: An opaque end-user identifier for the vendor's abuse tooling. openai only.

user.description: The vendor's older end-user identifier. openai only.

model.description: Per-model overrides, by the model id a request names. Overlaid field-wise over everything above: a set value replaces, and a list replaces whole. A per-model entry may not carry a `model` table of its own.

ServiceTier.title: Service tier
ServiceTier.description: The seat takes default, priority and ultrafast; the platform documents all six. `fast` is an alias of `priority`, rewritten at load and never sent.

context.description: How much of the conversation the model reasons over.

summary.description: How much of the reasoning comes back as readable summary. openai only: the wire already sends auto on both ids and the seat was never measured serving anything else.

mode.description: Which reasoning stack answers. openai only — the seat rejects pro and standard is already its default.

ReasoningContext.title: Reasoning context
ReasoningContext.description: How much of the conversation a reasoning model reasons over.

ReasoningSummary.title: Reasoning summary
ReasoningSummary.description: How much readable reasoning comes back.

TextOptions.title: Text options
TextOptions.description: `text` on a Responses request, minus `format` — which is `ganja run --json-schema`'s alone and is deliberately not a config key.

include_obfuscation.description: Whether text deltas carry the vendor's padding field. The wire already sends false on both Responses ids; a config setting it is setting it back.

ToolChoice.title: Tool choice
ToolChoice.description: What the model must call: a bare word, an allowed_tools narrowing, one named function, or a hosted tool. The hosted form is admitted on openai only — it is unprobed on the seat.

anyOf.title: Allowed tools
anyOf.description: A narrowed set the model picks from.

tools.description: The tools the model may pick from, in the vendor's own spelling.

anyOf.title: Named function
anyOf.description: One tool the model must call.

name.description: The tool that must be called.

anyOf.title: Hosted tool
anyOf.description: One vendor-run tool the model must call. openai only.

ServerToolEntry.title: Vendor-run tool
ServerToolEntry.description: One hosted tool, sent verbatim. `type` is validated per id — the seat registers web_search and image_generation, and shell, apply_patch and computer are refused on both ids because they need client-side execution. Every other key passes through, because the settings a hosted tool takes move when the vendor moves them.

type.description: The directive's kind; `compaction` is the one the vendor documents.

compact_threshold.description: How many tokens the backend lets the transcript reach first.

comparison_response_id.description: The response whose cache this request continues.

Truncation.title: Truncation
Truncation.description: What to do with a request that overflows the window.
